item.title: All Blacks overwhelm Wallabies with six-try first half
item.description: New Zealand scored six tries before halftime and beat Australia 43-21 in Sydney, extending its winning streak in the rivalry to 13 matches. The All Blacks led 36-7 at the break and retained the Bledisloe Cup for a 24th year.

item.title: NFL clears Josh Jacobs for Week 7 return
item.description: The NFL said Green Bay running back Josh Jacobs will come off the commissioner exempt list Monday and may play Oct. 25 at Detroit. Broncos linebacker Jonathon Cooper also was cleared to return for Week 7.

item.title: Real Madrid demands La Liga president resign
item.description: Real Madrid called for Javier Tebas to leave his posts at La Liga and Spain's football federation after he compared the club's media tactics with Nazi-era propaganda. The clash deepens a long-running feud over referees, governance and the Super League.

item.title: Brewers sweep Dodgers to reach first World Series since 1982
item.description: Milwaukee erased a 4-0 deficit to beat Los Angeles 6-4, complete an NLCS sweep and claim its first pennant in 44 years. Garrett Mitchell hit the go-ahead homer, Jake Bauers was named series MVP and the Brewers earned home field for the World Series.

item.title: Guardians take 2-1 ALCS lead behind Halpin homer
item.description: Petey Halpin hit a go-ahead two-run homer and Cleveland pitchers struck out 13 in a 3-2 win over Tampa Bay. The Guardians now lead the ALCS 2-1 after holding the Rays to three hits, a significant turn after the series was tied a day earlier.

item.title: Saudi attack disrupts golf, cycling and tennis calendar
item.description: The Asian Tour postponed the Saudi International indefinitely and cycling officials cancelled the Urban World Championships after the deadly Riyadh airport attack. The Six Kings Slam was delayed and FIFAe Finals postponed, while organizers said the 2027 Asian Cup remains on schedule.

item.title: Brewers move one win from first World Series since 1982
item.description: A day after taking a 2-0 NLCS lead, Milwaukee made the development decisive: a 6-2 Game 3 win left the Brewers one victory from their first World Series since 1982. Jake Bauers won an 11-pitch duel with a go-ahead two-run homer, Garrett Mitchell followed with another, and rookie Robert Gasser threw five scoreless innings.

item.title: A.J. Brown returns to Patriots practice
item.description: New England opened the 21-day activation window for A.J. Brown, who practiced on a limited basis after missing four games with a high-ankle sprain. The three-time second-team All-Pro joined the Patriots in a June trade from Philadelphia. Cornerback Christian Gonzalez also returned on a limited basis and said he is ready for Sunday's Jets game.

item.title: FIFA leaders confront Infantino after failed World Cup stake sale
item.description: Gianni Infantino faces a FIFA Council meeting after his proposal to sell investors a stake in a commercial subsidiary holding tournament rights collapsed. The heads of UEFA, the AFC and CONCACAF have called for him to resign. Reuters reports that opponents, while unlikely to replace him soon, aim to isolate him and curb his powers.

item.title: Rays even ALCS behind Freddy Peralta's gem
item.description: Tampa Bay beat Cleveland 3-1 to even the ALCS at one game apiece, a significant turn after the Guardians took the opener. Freddy Peralta worked six scoreless innings, and a José Ramírez error opened the door for a three-run fourth capped by Liam Hicks' two-run single.

item.title: Tkachuk brothers make NHL history in Panthers win
item.description: Brady Tkachuk scored a natural hat trick in 8:03 of the second period and Matthew assisted on all three goals as Florida beat Columbus 7-3. According to the NHL, Matthew became the first player to assist on each goal of a brother's natural hat trick; he finished with five assists.

item.title: U.S. soccer audiences keep growing after World Cup
item.description: Nielsen says 66.4 million U.S. viewers watched Spain beat Argentina in the World Cup final, the country's largest soccer audience. The momentum carried into club play: MLS viewing among men 18-34 rose 55%, Premier League viewing among young adults climbed 30%, and LaLiga's total audience increased 42%.

item.title: Bills outlast Rams in overtime thriller
item.description: Tyler Bass kicked a 45-yard field goal with 1:55 left in overtime as Buffalo edged Los Angeles 37-34. Josh Allen threw for 210 yards and ran for 121 more, while James Cook added 111 rushing yards and two touchdowns. The Rams forced overtime despite Buffalo leading 31-20 in the fourth quarter.

item.title: Brewers seize 2-0 NLCS lead over Dodgers
item.description: In a major follow-up to Milwaukee’s Game 1 win, William Contreras homered to tie Game 2, drove in the go-ahead run an inning later and finished with three hits and three RBIs in a 7-4 victory. Four Brewers relievers retired all 15 batters they faced, sending the NLCS to Los Angeles with Milwaukee ahead 2-0.

item.title: Guardians break late for ALCS Game 1 win
item.description: Cleveland scored seven runs over the final four innings to beat Tampa Bay 7-3 in the ALCS opener. Nathaniel Lowe’s two-run single in the eighth broke a 2-2 tie, and José Ramírez drove in a run for the fourth straight postseason game. The Guardians finished with 14 hits.
